title: Why You Get Goosebumps
hook: Cold air, or a song that hits just right, and your skin bristles for a reason older than language.
description: A short why-it-happens explainer of the reflex behind goosebumps, from the tiny muscles to the furry ancestors you no longer resemble.

scenes.vo: Cold air, or a song that hits just right, and your arms break out in tiny bumps.
scenes.caption: A song hits right and your arms break out in bumps.
scenes.whyArt: wide shot of a person reacting, forearm raised to the skin

scenes.vo: It feels like your skin is only reacting to the cold. That is half the story.
scenes.caption: It feels like just the cold. That is only half of it.
scenes.whyArt: simple sketch: thermometer crossed, a lightning bolt for feeling

scenes.vo: Deep in your fight-or-flight wiring, tiny muscles tug each hair straight up from its follicle.
scenes.caption: Tiny muscles tug each hair straight up from its follicle.
scenes.whyArt: close-in diagram of the arrector muscle at a hair root

scenes.vo: Furry animals do the exact same thing. Raised fur traps warm air and makes them look bigger.
scenes.caption: Furry animals do this too. Raised fur traps heat, looks bigger.
scenes.whyArt: worked example: a cat bristling versus a human arm

scenes.vo: You lost most of the fur. The reflex stayed. So a cold breeze still leaves its mark.
scenes.caption: You lost the fur. The reflex stayed. The bumps are left over.
scenes.whyArt: comparison: furry ancestor versus bare human arm, same bump
